findings.title: Wisdom as source-correcting restraint
findings.claim: Because bestowed wisdom is followed at once by a command to thank, the focus can present discernment as beginning in recognition of the giver. The wider scenes of David and Solomon receiving knowledge and naming favor, and of a ruler claiming power after receiving dominion, make gratitude legible as a restraint against treating a gift as self-originating.
findings.mechanism: The focus's gift of wisdom and imperative of gratitude are the carriers. In 27:15 and 27:19, bestowed knowledge is answered with praise, thanks, and a request to act rightly; 27:40 makes a received favor a test of thanks or denial and repeats the self-benefit maxim; 2:258 supplies a contrasting recipient who claims life-giving power after dominion is given. These contacts make gratitude the source-aware use of received wisdom.
findings.reader_payoff: Wisdom appears as practiced orientation: it keeps the source of a gift visible and governs how the recipient uses it.
findings.containment: The parallel scenes do not identify Luqman with Solomon, establish direct literary borrowing, or reduce wisdom to gratitude. The ruler in 2:258 is a contrastive example, not a judgment about Luqman; the focus's plain gift and command remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and their glosses are supplied; the cross-ayah comparison is an inference from exact target Arabic and nominated connection notes, while reader-walk support is legacy_unbound.

findings.title: The giver's independence and the receiver's recognition
findings.claim: The focus makes gratitude beneficial to the self while naming Allah independent and praiseworthy. The wider contexts join those attributes to God's ownership of all that is in the heavens and earth, then picture gratitude as recognition of signs while a ship moves by His favor. Together they make the self-benefit a human yield of recognition, not a payment needed by the giver.
findings.mechanism: The focus's gratitude, self-beneficiary, independence, and praise clauses carry the reading. 31:26 places ownership before the repeated independent-and-praiseworthy attributes; 31:31 places a vessel moving by divine favor beside signs and the patient-grateful response. The contact explains the asymmetry: the giver remains independent while gratitude is the recipient's capacity to recognize favor under changing conditions.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why gratitude benefits the self: it shapes how the recipient reads provision and signs, while the source does not depend on that response.
findings.containment: The maritime image belongs to 31:31, not to the focus scene. The patient and grateful may be types of observers rather than one person across a single trajectory; the wider echo does not turn every gratitude act into a sea journey.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective synthesis and both HFT context traces are legacy_unbound; the cited Arabic and the focus branches keep the comparison bounded.

findings.title: Ingratitude as post-rescue re-covering
findings.claim: The focus's contrast between gratitude and kufr can be heard as a change on the receiver's side: 31:32 moves from sincere appeal under engulfing danger to rescue and then to a differentiated aftermath that includes denial, betrayal, and ingratitude. The wider 64:6 echo again places divine independence and praise after rejection, so re-covering favor changes the responder while the source remains praiseworthy.
findings.mechanism: The focus gratitude and favor-denial branches are the carriers. In 31:32, engulfment is followed by rescue and then knowledgeable denial and ingratitude; 64:6 supplies another rejection followed by Allah's independent and praiseworthy attributes. The contact makes the focus's kufr branch a possible covering of known favor after conditions change, while the divine attributes bound the result.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the closing attributes matter after kufr: the refusal changes the receiver's relation to favor, not the giver's independence or worth.
findings.containment: The people who call during danger may not be the same individuals as those who are ungrateful after rescue; the reading is a sequence of possibilities, not a claim about one person's conversion. The covering sense is contained within the focus's ordinary ingratitude sense.

epistemic.reason: The context traces and focus branches are supplied, but HFT mappings are legacy_unbound; 64:6 is a nominated connection with target Arabic and no target morphology.

findings.title: Relational gratitude, nontransferable yield
findings.claim: The focus's self-benefit does not make gratitude solitary: a wider scene pairs thanks for divine and parental gifts with righteous action, while 31:33 says neither a parent nor a child can stand in for the other. The self that benefits remains the person who responds, even within close relationships.
findings.mechanism: The focus gratitude and self branches are the carriers. 46:15 joins thanks to God and parents with good action; 31:33 then denies parent–child substitution. Their contact makes gratitude relationally formed while keeping its consequence with the acting self.
findings.reader_payoff: The self-benefit clause can be understood without reducing it to private self-interest: close relationships matter, while responsibility remains personal.
findings.containment: The 31:33 clauses may address judgment generally and do not by themselves define the yield of gratitude. The 46:15 scene supplies a parallel relation; it does not prove a direct link between the two events.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is legacy_unbound; the parental-gratitude connection supplies exact Arabic but no target morphology.

findings.title: Wisdom as orientation without forecast
findings.claim: The focus's bestowed wisdom and self-directed benefit can be read as orientation for a response whose future outcome the self cannot forecast. 31:34 denies each self knowledge of tomorrow's gain and place of death; in contact with the focus's call to gratitude, that limit makes wisdom practical direction within uncertainty rather than possession of tomorrow.
findings.mechanism: The focus wisdom and own-self branches are the carriers. 31:34 repeats that no self knows its next day's earning or where it will die; the HFT trace also maps an exploratory path-and-wind alignment branch at those knowing words. Their contact bounds what the focus's wisdom and gratitude can promise.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see wisdom as a way to answer well within what is unknown, not a promise of predictive control.
findings.containment: The supplied alternative remains live: 31:34 may state divine omniscience without revising the practical meaning of 31:12. The path-alignment mapping is an attributed exploratory overlay, not an independent lexicon gloss; the focus's command to be grateful remains clear.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates and focus returns are exact, but the path-alignment branch is explicitly non-dominant and attributed, and the link from future limits to practical wisdom is inferential.

findings.title: Gratitude enacted through capacity
findings.claim: A wider use of the same gratitude word makes the focus's command concrete as action: the household of David is told to work in gratitude, and Solomon asks to be enabled to thank for received favor and do righteous work.
findings.mechanism: The focus gratitude word is the carrier. 34:13 pairs the gratitude form with a command to work; 27:19 joins a prayer for gratitude to a prayer for righteous action. Their contact activates the focus branch's behavioral facet and makes gratitude usable through what the recipient does.
findings.reader_payoff: Gratitude can be understood as a response enacted through received ability, not only as spoken acknowledgment.
findings.containment: The wider scenes add an enacted form of gratitude without excluding praise or inward recognition from the focus's ordinary sense.

epistemic.reason: The target Arabic and connection notes are supplied, but target morphology is not; the connection remains a contextual interpretation.

findings.title: The self as the return of action
findings.claim: The focus's phrase for one's own self belongs to a wider pattern in which the yield of an act returns to its agent: another verse applies the same self-return to striving, and two others pair good done for the self with harm returned against it. The focus's gratitude is one instance of this relation, not a private benefit detached from action.
findings.mechanism: The focus's self-beneficiary phrase is the carrier. 29:6 repeats the self-return form for striving and says God has no need of the worlds; 41:46 and 45:15 repeat the relation for good and harmful action. Their contact makes the focus's self-benefit an agent-side consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the benefit of gratitude belongs to the person whose response it forms; it does not supply anything Allah lacks.
findings.containment: The parallel does not equate gratitude with striving or every deed with the same outcome. It generalizes the self-return relation while leaving the focus's named act intact.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows supply exact Arabic and direct authored notes, but their target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.activation: The repeated same-self relation meets the focus beneficiary and makes the result belong to the agent rather than the giver.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The gratitude benefit is an instance of a wider return of action to its doer.

findings.title: The self as inward witness
findings.claim: A wider use of nafs opens the focus's self-benefit toward inward moral life: one passage links forgetting God to forgetting one's own self, and another names a self that reproaches itself. Beside the focus, these echoes allow the benefit to include a person's capacity to recognize and answer their own position.
findings.mechanism: The focus's own-self word is the carrier. 59:19 links forgetting God with self-forgetting; 75:2 names a self-reproaching soul. These independent uses meet the focus's self-beneficiary and its gratitude/kufr contrast, shifting the self from a bare recipient toward an inward moral witness.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the self that benefits as a person who also recognizes, forgets, or reproaches their own response.
findings.containment: The focus still uses nafs as the actor's self and beneficiary. This is an exploratory resonance, not a claim that the word means conscience in 31:12 or that gratitude guarantees a particular inward state.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic contexts repeat the self word and give a concrete moral relation, but the inward-witness contact is an analogical inference and target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: Praise beyond the human response
findings.claim: The focus names Allah praiseworthy after describing human ingratitude; a wider verse says that the heavens, earth, and everything within them glorify Him with praise. The echo makes the focus's final epithet reach beyond the response of the human recipient.
findings.mechanism: The focus praiseworthiness adjective is the carrier. 17:44 supplies universal glorification with the same praise root, independently of the focus's human gratitude/kufr pair. The contact expands the frame from one recipient's response to praise surrounding creation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the giver's praiseworthiness does not depend on whether this recipient gives thanks.
findings.containment: Glorification and the focus's praiseworthiness remain distinct expressions. The wider verse does not say that all creation gives human-style gratitude or explain the self-benefit clause.

epistemic.reason: The target Arabic repeats the praise root and the connection note identifies the wider relation, but target morphology is not supplied.
